newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-CHAVEZ PICKS UP 100TH WIN IN NON-TITLE BOUT.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-CHAVEZ PICKS UP 100TH WIN IN NON-TITLE BOUT.

text.p: Former world champions Julio Cesar Chavez of Mexico and countryman Miguel Angel Gonzalez recorded convincing victories Saturday to set up a showdown for the vacant World Boxing Council super lightweight title later this year.
Chavez recorded the 100th victory of his illustrious 18-year professional career with a 10-round unanimous decision in a non-title bout with journeyman Larry Daniel La Coursiere.

Gonzalez earlier halted Roberto Granciosa of the Philippines after the third round of their scheduled 10-round bout. Both fights were on the undercard of the Mike Tyson-Evander Holyfield World Boxing Association heavyweight title rematch.
Chavez, the WBC super lightweight champion from 1990-1996, knocked down La Coursiere in the fourth with a right to the head and breezed from there.
Chavez, 34, won by scores of 100-89 on two of the judges' scorecards, and by 99-90 on the third judge's card to raise his record to 100-2-1. La Coursiere, 31, fell to 22-7-1.
"I will look better and be prepared when I fight for the title," promised an overweight Chavez.
"It was boring for me. I am ready for a world title fight. I apologise that I was not in the best condition."
Gonzalez, the WBC lightweight champion from 1992 until earlier this year, battered Granciosa at will, prompting referee Jay Nady to halt the one-sided bout between the third and fourth rounds.
The 26-year-old Gonzalez raised his record to 42-1, while Granciosa, 31, dropped to 31-18-3.
"This fight prepared me for Chavez," Gonzalez said.
"I will be ready for Chavez and I will win by a knockout."
